s2.key: af_heart|0.8|Every how-to video plays at the same speed, whether you keep up, or not.

s3a.key: af_heart|0.8|Falls are the second-leading cause of unintentional injury death worldwide.

s3b.key: af_heart|0.8|In one survey, three in four people didn't finish their home physical therapy exercises.

s3c.key: af_heart|0.8|And most cardiac arrests outside hospital happen at home, where nobody is checking your form.

s4a.key: af_heart|0.8|At least nine in ten deaf children are born to hearing parents.

s4b.key: af_heart|0.8|And a video can't see whether your hands are right.

s5.key: af_heart|0.8|In Step is the video that waits for you.

s6a.key: af_heart|0.8|Prop up your phone. It becomes the camera: an external camera, not the TV.

s6b.key: af_heart|0.8|Pose tracking runs in the phone's browser. Only body points travel to the TV, never video.

s7a.key: af_heart|0.8|At each key moment, the lesson pauses, and continues only when your pose is right.

s7b.key: af_heart|0.8|It counts your reps, times your balance, and if you're stuck, a coach gives one short, kind tip.

s8.key: af_heart|0.8|Safety comes first: no balance work until a chair is beside you. And if the camera drops, the lesson stops.

s9a.key: af_heart|0.8|The same engine teaches sign-language hand shapes, hand rehab, and CPR rhythm: practice only, not certification.

s9b.key: af_heart|0.8|Kids act out a story. And two people can practise together.

s10a.key: af_heart|0.8|A physiotherapist or teacher records a lesson once, on a phone.

s10b.key: af_heart|0.8|In Step finds the still moments, suggests the steps, and publishes it to the TV.

s11a.key: af_heart|0.8|Under the hood: an open lesson format, called dot eye step,

s11b.key: af_heart|0.8|One pure TypeScript gate engine, shared by the phone, the server, and the TV, decides when to move on.

s11c.key: af_heart|0.8|And the gated video player is open source, for any Vega app.

s12.key: af_heart|0.8|In Step. The video that waits for you.

cam_a.key: af_heart|0.8|Prop up your phone or laptop. It becomes the camera: an external camera, not the TV.

cam_b.key: af_heart|0.8|Pose tracking runs in its browser. Only body points travel to the TV: numbers, never video.

heel_a.key: af_heart|0.8|This is Fall Prevention, on the Vega Virtual Device. At each key moment, the lesson pauses, and continues only when your pose is right.

heel_b.key: af_heart|0.8|It counts your reps and times your balance. If you're stuck, it offers one short, kind tip.

safe.key: af_heart|0.8|Safety comes first. No balance work until a chair is beside you. And if the camera drops, the lesson stops, and waits.

asl_a.key: af_heart|0.8|Sign Language for Families teaches hand shapes, letter by letter.

asl_b.key: af_heart|0.8|The hands are illustrated, and not yet reviewed by Deaf signers. Learn with Deaf teachers, too.

kids_a.key: af_heart|0.8|For kids, the lesson is a story.

kids_b.key: af_heart|0.8|The forest waits until they're a tree, a mouse, and a flamingo.

more_a.key: af_heart|0.8|The same engine runs hand rehab, and CPR rhythm: practice only, not certification.

more_b.key: af_heart|0.8|And two people can practise together, each with their own phone.

file.key: af_heart|0.8|Every lesson is an open file, called dot eye step: a video, plus the poses it waits for.

arch_a.key: af_heart|0.8|The phone sends body points over a WebSocket. A small server relays them to the TV.

hon.key: af_heart|0.8|No learner video leaves the phone. The voices are synthetic, made on this machine. And the AWS coach is built, but switched off.
